neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were involved in an altercation after consuming liquor. The accused assaulted the victim, resulting in the victim's death. The accused was found with blood-stained clothes and had injuries consistent with the assault. The victim's body showed multiple injuries, including fractures and lacerations. The accused was medically examined and found to have injuries that matched the time of the incident. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including the accused's extra judicial confession and medical reports, to establish the accused's involvement in the victim's death.

quotes.text: J.P. Tiwari, Sanjeev Bansal, Praksh Kumar Singh for the Appellant. Nupur Choudhary (for Kamal Mohan Gupta) for the Respondent.
The Investigating Officer submitted charge sheet against accused Sanjeev (appellant) for his trial in respect of offence punishable under Section 302 IPC.

value.supreme_court: Conviction and sentence under Section 302 IPC set aside; convicted under Section 304 Part I IPC

quotes.text: The conviction and sentence recorded by the trial court and affirmed by the High Court in respect of offence punishable under Section 302 IPC against the appellant, is set aside.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused had an altercation with the victim after consuming liquor, assaulted the victim, resulting in the victim's death. The prosecution's evidence included the extra judicial confession made by the accused to a witness, corroborated by the statement of the doctor, establishing that the act committed by the accused is covered by Exception 4 to s. 300 and is punishable under s. 304 Part I.

quotes.text: The prosecution evidence relating to extra judicial confession made before PW-12 is believed by the courts below to examine as to whether act committed by the accused constitutes culpable homicide amounting to murder or not.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no motive for the accused to commit murder and that the prosecution's circumstantial evidence did not complete the chain of circumstances, leading to an erroneous conviction under s. 302.

quotes.text: It is further argued that the circumstances shown by the prosecution in the present case do not complete the chain, and the courts below have erred in law in holding the appellant guilty of the charge of murder.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that to determine culpable homicide, the courts must examine the circumstances to infer the intention or knowledge of the accused, and that motive is not a necessary element to prove murder.

quotes.text: In order to read either intention or knowledge to commit the crime, the courts have to examine the circumstances, as there cannot be any direct evidence as to the state of mind of the accused.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the act committed by the accused falls under Exception 4 to s. 300 IPC, which covers culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and thus is punishable under s. 304 Part I.

quotes.text: The act committed by the appellant in the present case is covered by Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC, i.e., culpable homicide not amounting to murder, as such the same is, punishable under Section 304 Part I, IPC.

other_sentence_order.value: The appellant was sentenced to ten years imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 5000/-, and in default of payment of fine, he was directed to undergo further imprisonment for a period of two months.

quotes.text: The appellant is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of ten years and to pay fine of Rs.5000/-, in default of which the appellant shall undergo imprisonment for a further period of two months.
